report:
Reviewed the complete expansion-completeness claim, all eight implementation associations and all five test entries. Captured the modules design, terminal-incompleteness RFD, in-memory harness/root setup and trait lookup helpers. Source inspection only; no test reruns or source edits.

The claim distinguishes safe represented symbols from exhaustive absence, requiring completeness for the specific semantic question. mods.rs publishes represented expanded items while separately computing trait-, method-provider- and symbol-listing completeness. Its bang-macro check treats unresolved definitions, active unexpanded attributes, malformed/error items and depth limits conservatively and recursively checks nested expansion. macro_invocations.rs converts expansion failure into an Error item instead of an empty successful expansion. builtins.rs returns None for unsupported derive/input shapes; mods.rs interprets derive incompleteness in relation to the queried trait rather than universally equating an unsupported unrelated builtin with hidden target impls. local_impl_candidates in impls.rs accumulates module completeness and incomplete/missing impl facts across discovery. clauses.rs propagates this uncertainty into candidate assembly. prove.rs carries it alongside candidate answers to merge_candidate_results. merge.rs allows a definite unconditional proof to win, but empty candidate absence becomes No only when no incomplete source was seen; otherwise anti_unify.rs merge_hints produces conservative combined uncertainty rather than relying on an exhaustive candidate list. These eight entries cover publication and the solver-negative consequence without claiming every semantic consumer is fully tested.

The ordinary no_candidates_is_no_only_for_complete_source test asserts No for an empty complete candidate set and Maybe for an empty incomplete set. unconditional_yes_wins_over_incomplete_source supplies an actual empty-substitution, trivially true Proven answer via its in-file yes helper and requires Yes despite incompleteness. Thus both halves of the claim have direct merge-level assertions.

The two source-driven tests request a ground Bool:Marker proof after obtaining the represented Marker trait from expanded items. unresolved_item_macro_prevents_ground_no uses missing!(); malformed_item_macro_output_prevents_ground_no_without_panicking uses macro output consisting of malformed impl syntax. Both assert QueryResultData::Maybe. The captured harness creates and parses a real local root; trait_and_crate selects the actual published trait. These tests show represented symbols remain available and incomplete expansion prevents a false exhaustive negative for these two cases. They do not establish every unsupported/resource-limited scenario or every semantic question.

The explicit modules_expand_completeness TODO retains the broader end-to-end matrix: successful expansion permitting ground negative answers, and unresolved, malformed, unsupported and resource-limited expansion yielding conservative uncertainty. Completing those remaining source-driven cases and question-specific completeness coverage is its prerequisite. It contains no assertions and is not counted as ordinary proof; the merge tests do not substitute for a successful-expansion integration case. All entries and claim qualifications are accounted for, no concrete defect was identified in these paths, and no additional edits are requested.
